toast.deployStarted: Deploying {{name}} — check the Deploys tab for progress
toast.deployBusy: Another deploy for {{name}} is already running{{reason}}

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.content: The app and its current Docker container will be removed.

redeployPrompt.title: Redeploy {{name}} now?
redeployPrompt.content: Config is saved, but the running container still has the old config. Redeploying will pull the new image, restart the container, and refresh the Caddy reverse proxy.

editor.name: Name
editor.namePattern: Must start with a-z and contain only lowercase letters, digits, dashes
editor.nameExtra: Used as Docker container / compose project prefix.
editor.composePathExtra: If set, overrides the inline content below. Use an absolute path the nanoku process can read.
editor.composeContentRequired: Provide a compose file path or inline YAML
editor.composeContentExtra: Multi-service stacks are supported. Container names will be prefixed with the app name.
editor.exposedPortsHint: Declare which compose services Caddy should be able to reverse-proxy to. Without this, sites can only use a custom upstream.
editor.exposedPortExtra: Container-side port. The Caddyfile will use nanoku-<app>-<name>-1:<port>.
editor.exposedPortImportTooltip: Parse the app's stored compose YAML and pre-fill the list. You'll review / edit before saving.
editor.exposedPortImportNeedsPort: Imported {{total}} services; {{need}} have no detectable port — please fill them in.
editor.portExtra: Port the app listens on inside the container.
editor.deleteVolumesOnRemove: Delete auto-named volumes when app is removed
editor.deleteVolumesOnRemoveExtra: Only nanoku-managed volumes (nanoku-<app>-vol-*) are touched. Bind mounts and user-named volumes are always kept.
editor.envVarsHint: Override any same-named variables baked into the image.
editor.volumesHint: Docker mode only. Named volumes are auto-created; auto-named volumes can be cleaned up when the app is removed.

registry.title: Private registry (optional)
registry.collapsedHint: Disabled. Turn on to enter the registry URL and credentials.
registry.passwordExtra: Stored encrypted at rest is on the roadmap; currently stored in the SQLite DB.

trigger.enableExtra: Generates a per-app bearer token. Any system that can produce a JSON POST and compute a Bearer header (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Drone, local scripts) can fire a deploy.
trigger.disabledHint: Trigger is not enabled. Re-create the app to enable it.
trigger.collapsedHint: Disabled. Turn on to enable on create, or to view the trigger URL (when already enabled).
trigger.offWhileEnabledHint: Turning off clears the trigger token. Turning it back on generates a new one.
trigger.editNotEnabledHint: Trigger is not enabled. Flip the switch on and save to enable — a new token will be generated.
trigger.disableHint: Turning it off clears the token; turning it back on issues a new one (old token stops working immediately).
trigger.rotateDescription: A new random token will be generated. The old token stops working immediately.
trigger.rotateDescriptionShort: A new random token will be generated. You'll see it once.
trigger.tokenWarning: Copy the token now. You won't be able to see it again.
trigger.protocolGuide: Send POST to the URL above with Authorization: Bearer <token> and a JSON body of { "tag": "<sha>", "commit_message": "<msg>" }. The tag is appended to the app's image (the part before the :).
trigger.usagePlaceholder: The curl below reads the token from the env var {{var}} — set it in your CI's secret store. The workflow YAML references the same name as a GitHub Actions secret.
trigger.curlTitle: Generic shell snippet — works from any CI

emptyState.title: No apps yet
emptyState.subtitle: Add your first app to deploy a container.

detail.rollbackConfirmDesc: This re-pulls the image from deploy #{{id}} and runs it as the new container. The current container will be retired.
detail.deleteVolumesOnRemove: Clean up auto-named volumes on app removal
detail.composeModeHint: Compose mode — edit volumes in the compose YAML instead.

volumeEditor.autoHint: Empty source → nanoku auto-names it as nanoku-<app>-vol-<n>
